paragraphs: Being willing to check the denominator, the period and the source of a single energy-saving figure and to explain the result to non-technical colleagues is the signal worth trying; merely liking environmental slogans is not enough to judge whether you can carry metrics and proposal work.

Judge interest in sustainability topics, spreadsheet analysis, communication and the actual post conditions separately. The U.S. O*NET places this at Job Zone 4, usually with considerable education and preparation; the example Chinese internship post requires a bachelor's degree or above, which is not a uniform national threshold.

First distinguish the two work lines of metrics and proposal analysis, and communication and implementation. The first needs reliable data and cost feasibility judgments, the second needs plans, feedback and cross-department coordination, and both share facts and responsibility boundaries.

Use the entry module F1 fictional office data, the F2 A and B feedback and the F3 six-column record for the experience. Pen and paper or an ordinary spreadsheet is enough; check the eight claims, without collecting real company data, purchasing equipment or issuing zero-carbon certification.
What kind of person is sustainability work suited to?

First see whether you can read energy or waste metrics clearly, find data differences, compare cost and feasibility, and then explain the known results and unconfirmed conditions clearly. The post also requires coordinating with management, operations, procurement and staff and maintaining plans and reports continuously, not just writing one promotional article.
This is an exploration screening, not a professional assurance, qualification certification or hiring conclusion; one fictional exercise only helps choose the next learning task.

Observable signals include: checking per-capita intensity further when the total falls, not deciding for management when the budget is exceeded, keeping the unknowns when data is missing, and being able to point out which number, sentence or condition was changed after feedback. You are also willing to explain the proposal cost, the expected effect and the implementation responsibility, and not to write an estimate as actual performance.

If repeated table checking is hard to accept, if you habitually draw an environmental conclusion first and then look for data, or if you think generating a report equals completing organisational improvement, verify these habits first. The workplace, project deadlines, communication language and data availability are checked against the specific post and are not decided by personality labels.

After completing F1 to F3, compare the first draft, version A, version B and the final: were the four errors corrected, does each of the eight judgments have a basis, and are the emission factors and the approval status still recorded as unknown. Then decide whether to keep learning metric analysis, sustainability projects or the related post conditions.

This page uses O*NET-SOC 13-1199.05 Sustainability Specialists as the occupational identity: handling an organisation's waste streams, green building, green purchasing and similar sustainability topics. Not every investment, audit or promotional post with an ESG name is the same as this occupation.

Inputs include energy and resource use, waste and recycling records, policy proposals, technical and market material and organisational objectives. The editorial suggestion is to register the period, units, boundary, source and denominator first, and not to mix data from different scopes.

Monitoring metrics and evaluating proposals are connected: the first shows what happened, the second compares cost effectiveness, technical feasibility and acceptability. Absolute totals, intensity and projected effects should be kept apart, and a comprehensive improvement is not declared from one falling figure.

Outputs include project objectives, metric ledgers, sustainability plans, proposals, reports and presentations, and staff training or communication material. Quality is whether the material is traceable, the calculations are reviewable, the limitations are clear and decisions can be supported, not just the layout.

O*NET lists tasks such as creating metrics, tracking energy resources and waste streams, reviewing policies and investigating environmental policy violations. Material conflicts should keep the original version and be confirmed with the corresponding data owner; measured values must not be invented to complete a report.

Collaborate with sustainability professionals, managers, operations and procurement and staff, and possibly provide technical or administrative support and secure project resources. Analysis and advice, budget approval, engineering implementation and external assurance are different responsibilities and are confirmed by the organisational division of work.

The work also includes regulatory, technical and market research, applying for funding, training and external communication. When recruiting, show how you verify, analyse and revise, and do not treat one generated text as a completed real project.

At delivery, state the material used, the metric definitions, the expected versus the actual, the conditions awaiting confirmation and the next responsibility. Public material requires separate permission; a training report is not a real organisational result or third-party certification.

Metrics and proposal analysis, and communication and project implementation, are the two internal work lines of this occupation. The order below is an editorial summary, and real organisations may iterate in parallel; the same specialist may also carry tasks on both lines.
Metrics and proposal analysis line
Confirm the objective → collect the records → define the metrics → check the calculations → compare cost and feasibility → form a recommendation
A metric ledger and proposal comparison with sources, units and limitations
Communication and project implementation line
Confirm the topic → coordinate stakeholders → maintain the plan → prepare reports and training → collect feedback → adjust the proposal
An executable plan, explanatory material and a feedback revision record
Common professional foundation
Material retrieval · metric basis · cost effectiveness · technical feasibility · organisational communication · traceable records
What is the difference between metric analysis and communication and implementation?

The first focuses on data definitions, calculations and the basis for proposals, the second on turning the basis into a plan the organisation can understand and execute. Both need fact checking; communication cannot write an expected saving that has not happened as actual abatement.
Core purpose
Let decision-makers understand the conditions of energy, resource and waste metrics and candidate proposals.
Let the relevant departments understand the objective, the division of work and the progress and support implementation and adjustment of the proposal.

The specialist coordinates and explains, management or the designated lead approves, and operations or engineering staff implement according to their duties.

Calculating a fictional saving rate correctly does not prove real emissions, technical acceptance or valid external assurance.
Writing a good plan does not mean the budget has been approved, the proposal implemented or the organisation certified.
Key occupational judgments

The questions below are used to check the metrics, the proposal and the responsibility; answers go back to the original records and the specific task, and promotional effects are not equated with professional output.
What are the units, periods and denominators of this period's total and per-capita intensity?
Is the proposal effect an observed result or an unimplemented estimate?
Have the budget, technical feasibility and organisational acceptability been checked separately?
Which metric, clause or statement does the feedback ask to be changed?
Restate the specific objective first, locate the figure and the original text, and keep the version; keep asking about vague comments and do not just replace the wording with something greener.
Does the external environmental statement have an original basis and professional confirmation?
Without emission factors or assurance, do not announce abatement tonnage or certification; the public use, approval and professional responsibility of the material are checked separately.

A sustainability specialist can analyse and coordinate at the same time; the chief officer, engineering manager, biofuel R&D manager and water resource specialist each have independent deliverables and responsibilities, and participating in the same project does not mean they are interchangeable.

Use F1 first to judge whether you prefer tracing data or explaining proposals, then check the weighting of the two lines in a real post. When moving to a management or specialist technical occupation, prove the ability with the target outputs and do not treat specialist years as a pass.

Does finishing a report with AI prove energy saving?

No. The report still has to be checked against the measurement records, the boundary and the period; proposal estimates and post-implementation measurements are kept apart. A model being able to write a conclusion does not mean the energy quantity, the denominator or the emission factor is correct.
Does potential exposure equal actual layoffs?

No. The ILO describes task potential, and adoption depends on data, processes, cost and responsibility. Without adoption and outcome evidence for this occupation, a specialist unemployment rate cannot be calculated.
Can AI replace the occupational tasks and quality requirements?

No. O*NET lists tasks such as metric tracking, proposal evaluation, plan reporting and training; a generated draft is only a possible assisted step. The input, the calculation, the feasibility and the responsibility must be checked, and generating text cannot be used to infer that all deliverables are complete.

Does parent occupation growth prove that AI has no effect?

No. Total growth and task change can happen at the same time; the parent occupation 3.9% covers many occupations and factors and does not support a net AI loss or a personal hiring probability for this occupation.
Does knowing Excel, Power BI or LCA mean using AI professionally?

No. The software background, metric knowledge and generative output checking are different abilities. Check the data and formulas first, then the draft source; proficiency with tool commands also does not prove the conclusion or the certification authority is valid.
What should be checked before using an external tool?

Check the organisational data permission, whether the material is unpublished, the service retention method and the review responsibility. The training uses only the F1 fictional data; real client, staff or supplier material is handled under unit rules.

values: F1 | Fictional office energy briefing

Paper training only: the same office, two months of equal length, the same measurement scope. R1 base period 1000 kilowatt-hours and 100 people; R2 current period 900 kilowatt-hours and 75 people, both given observations. Total change=(current−base)/base; per-capita quantity=electricity/headcount, per-capita change=(current per-capita−base per-capita)/base per-capita.

R3 two mutually exclusive proposals for the next period, with a monthly budget cap of 500 yuan: A costs 600 yuan per month and is estimated to save 100 kilowatt-hours per month; B costs 400 yuan per month and is estimated to save 80 kilowatt-hours per month. The costs and effects are both given estimates and do not prove implementation; the savings of A and B must not be added. No electricity price, emission factor, approval, real technical conditions or external assurance is given.
F2 | The wrong draft and independent feedback

The same wrong draft D: 'this period's electricity use fell 20% and the per-capita figure improved 10%. Choosing A fits the 500 yuan budget, and the office has obtained zero-carbon certification.' A feedback: check only the total and per-capita ratios, at least two revisions; B feedback: start independently from D and check only the budget choice and the certification, at least two revisions; finally merge the four corrections.

J1 check the input units and period; J2 the total change; J3 the per-capita quantity; J4 the per-capita change; J5 the budget and the mutually exclusive choice; J6 the observation and the proposal estimate; J7 whether emissions and certification can be confirmed; J8 whether approval and actual implementation can be confirmed. F3 lists 'judgment | input basis | first draft | A/B changes | final draft | basis and unknowns', one row for each of the eight items.
Reference answer | The eight judgments and the four revisions

J1 the same scope and equal-length months, using kilowatt-hours, headcount and yuan per month separately. J2 (900−1000)/1000=−10%. J3 base period 10 and current period 12 kilowatt-hours per person. J4 (12−10)/10=+20%, so per-capita intensity rose and cannot be called an improvement. J5 A exceeds the budget by 100 yuan and B leaves a balance of 100 yuan, so only B meets the given budget; mutually exclusive options cannot be added.

J6 the before and after electricity use are given observations, while the proposal saving of 80 is only an estimate and is not proven to have occurred. J7 without an emission factor and assurance, abatement tonnage cannot be calculated or zero-carbon certification confirmed. J8 the approval and implementation are unknown. A changes it to 'the total fell 10% and the per-capita figure rose 20%'; B changes it to 'only B fits the given budget, and there is no evidence to confirm zero-carbon certification'; the merged final keeps all four correct changes and all the unknowns, and does not derive technical approval from the cost budget.
